intended_object: The coordinate Hopf algebra A[G] of the closed subgroup scheme G ⊆ GL_{2^n} over A generated by the 2n positive and negative simple-root subgroups (copies of G_a) and the rank-n weight torus of the type-Dₙ spin representation. In other words, the smallest closed subgroup scheme through which all these morphisms factor. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the quotient of the coordinate Hopf algebra of GL_{2^n} over A by `generatedDefiningIdeal`. That ideal is `commonKernelHopfIdeal` of the generator coordinate maps, which is the supremum of all Hopf ideals killed by every generator, i.e. the largest Hopf ideal contained in the common kernel. Its `HopfIdeal` structure carries the standard conditions: Δ(I) ⊆ I⊗H + H⊗I, ε(I) = 0 and S(I) ⊆ I.

Closed subgroup schemes of GL correspond to Hopf ideals. So the quotient by the largest Hopf ideal killed by all the generators is the coordinate ring of the smallest closed subgroup scheme through which every generator factors. This is the standard scheme-theoretic notion of the subgroup generated by a family of homomorphisms (Milne, Algebraic Groups §2.h). Taking the supremum of Hopf ideals avoids assuming that ring-theoretic kernels are Hopf ideals, which can fail over non-flat bases. The module documentation is careful not to claim more, for instance equality with the base change of the integral carrier.

The generator index type `(Fin n ⊕ Fin n) ⊕ Unit` gives the 2n numbered root subgroups plus the torus, which matches the docstring. The base ring is an arbitrary commutative ring. This is a specific object (the spin group of type Dₙ inside GL_{2^n}), so a specific setting is not over-specialization. Mathlib has no counterpart for this group scheme or for the generated-subgroup construction on Hopf algebras.
